source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Assess the client, use required clinical and safety reporting channels, document factual care, and continue indicated monitoring.","B":"Withhold reporting unless the client later develops an injury or measurable adverse effect from the error.","C":"Complete the causal investigation independently before informing the care team or the organization’s safety process.","D":"Document routine medication administration and continue observation; formal event reporting can wait unless symptoms or injury emerge."}}
source_row.rationale: The 2026 NCSBN test plan includes acknowledging and documenting practice errors and near misses, reporting incidents/events, intervening or escalating safety concerns, and evaluating the client’s response. A no-harm outcome does not eliminate the need for assessment and required reporting.
source_row.source_detail: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — ‘Reporting of Incident/Event’ and practice-error/near-miss activities: acknowledge/document errors, report incidents, and evaluate client response. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Safe and Effective Care Environment — Safety and Infection Prevention and Control; Reporting of Incident/Event and infection/safety activities as applicable. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
source_row.stem: A medication error reaches a client, but immediate assessment shows no apparent injury. Which nursing response best supports patient safety?
